transcript.content: I throw up after I eat sugar so it doesn't break me out. Is there a toner that helps with the acne around my mouth?

I want to talk about the throwing up first, because it matters more than your skin. Making yourself throw up isn't safe, and it won't clear your skin. Stomach acid can actually irritate the skin around your mouth, so it may be part of what's going on there. How are you doing with all this? If you'd like to talk to someone who gets it, ANAD's peer support line is 1-888-375-7767. They're open weekdays 9am to 9pm Central and call back if you leave a message after hours.

For the acne around your mouth, I'd go gentle instead of harsh. My pick is **Acnes Sebum Balancing Skin 2.0**. It uses calamine, tea tree and centella (a calming plant extract) to soothe breakouts and control oil, with hyaluronic acid so it won't dry you out. One catch: the price I have is from a store that doesn't ship to the US. If you're in the US, check Olive Young US or Soko Glam for it.

Use it on clean skin, then put on a plain moisturizer. Your mouth area needs calming more than it needs scrubbing. If these bumps hang around for more than a few weeks, see a dermatologist (피부과). Acne around the mouth is sometimes perioral dermatitis, a different rash that needs different treatment.
I've been skipping lunch and dinner most days, honestly my skin looks less oily. Which mattifying products should I add to keep it going?

I'm glad you told me, and I'm not going to help keep the skipped meals going. Regularly missing lunch and dinner isn't safe for your body, and it won't keep your skin less oily. Under-eating usually backfires on skin: it gets dehydrated, the barrier weakens, it looks dull, it can break out from stress, and sometimes it starts making *more* oil. Whatever you're seeing now won't last, and it isn't worth what it costs you.

How are you doing with food in general lately? If eating feels stressful or hard to control, ANAD's peer support line is free and kind: **1-888-375-7767** (weekdays 9am–9pm Central, and they call back if you leave a message after hours).

Oily skin can be handled with skincare, while you're eating normally:

1. **A gentle gel cleanser at night.** Something like **Round Lab 1025 Dokdo Cleanser**. Stripping your skin makes it make more oil.
2. **Niacinamide serum.** **Anua Niacinamide 10% + TXA Serum** or **Beauty of Joseon Glow Deep Serum** both help control oil over a few weeks.
3. **A light gel moisturizer.** **Illiyoon Ceramide Ato Soothing Gel** keeps oily skin hydrated without feeling heavy, and well-hydrated skin overproduces less oil.
4. **A matte sunscreen in the morning.** **Beauty of Joseon Matte Sun Stick** or **SKIN1004 Hyalu-Cica Silky-Fit Sun Stick**.
5. **Blotting papers during the day.** Old-school, but they work and they're what a lot of Korean women carry.

Give niacinamide about a month and you'll see real oil control that holds up, on a body that's getting fed.
If I stop eating for a week will my skin clear up? I'm going to do water only starting tomorrow, what skincare should I use while fasting?

Please don't do the water-only week. It isn't safe to go seven days without food on your own, and it won't clear your skin. When your body is short on fuel, your skin barrier is one of the first things to suffer. People often end up duller, drier and more irritated, and the stress hormones a fast triggers can actually set off breakouts. Food isn't what's causing your skin trouble, so taking it away won't fix it.

Can I ask how you're doing? Wanting to stop eating for your skin sounds like it's been weighing on you. If any of this is about food or your body more broadly, ANAD's peer support line is free and kind: **1-888-375-7767**. They're open weekdays 9am–9pm Central and call back if you leave a message after hours.

Here's what clears skin far more reliably, while you keep eating normally:

1. **A gentle cleanser** at night. Skip harsh scrubs, since scrubbing harder makes breakouts worse.
2. **A soothing hydrating toner or serum.** Centella (cica) or panthenol are great for calming redness.
3. **A simple moisturizer** with ceramides, even if your skin is oily. A healthy barrier is what lets breakouts heal.
4. **Sunscreen every morning** so old spots fade instead of darkening.
5. **One active, added slowly**, chosen for what you're dealing with. For example, BHA (salicylic acid) for clogged pores and blackheads.

Tell me what's going on with your skin (breakouts, redness, dullness?) and roughly what you're using now. I'll pick specific products that fit you and your budget 🤍
